questions.question_text: Different species of Ephedra can be identified by observing the nature of
questions.explanation: Ephedra species are morphologically identified by examining the characteristics of their outer surface and stem striations.

questions.question_text: Indian Rhubarb can be distinguished from Rhapontic Rhubarb by the fluorescence it emits under UV light. Indian Rhubarb gives
questions.explanation: Indian rhubarb exhibits a deep violet fluorescence under UV light, distinguishing it from rhapontic rhubarb.

questions.question_text: Genetically modified species of Papaver namely Papaver bracteatum and Papaver orientale contain the predominant alkaloid
questions.explanation: Papaver bracteatum and Papaver orientale are well known to accumulate thebaine as their primary alkaloid instead of morphine.

questions.question_text: Increased risk of atherosclerosis is associated with decreased serum levels of
questions.explanation: HDL is known as 'good cholesterol' because it helps remove other forms of cholesterol from your bloodstream; low levels increase heart disease risk.

questions.question_text: A peptide hormone which inhibits bone resorption and given as nasal spray is
questions.explanation: Calcitonin is a peptide hormone that inhibits osteoclastic bone resorption and can be administered intranasally.

questions.question_text: An inorganic ion which is used prophylactically in bipolar depression is
questions.explanation: Lithium (as lithium carbonate) is the classic mood-stabilizing inorganic ion used for the prophylaxis and treatment of bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: A $\beta$-lactamase inhibitor which contains an $1$-oxopenam structure is
questions.explanation: Clavulanate potassium contains an oxopenam core ring system (specifically 1-oxopenam).

questions.question_text: Salbutamol is prepared from

options.A: OH-H2C-N-CH3 attached to a benzene ring

questions.explanation: Salbutamol synthesis typically starts from 4-hydroxy-3-hydroxymethylacetophenone.

questions.question_text: Antihypothrombinemic effect of one stereochemical form is two to five times more than others
questions.explanation: (S)-Warfarin is significantly more potent than (R)-warfarin as an anticoagulant.

questions.question_text: Some of the organic reactions are catalysed by a product obtained from starch on treatment with amylase from Bacillus macerans. It is
questions.explanation: Cyclodextrins are produced by the action of cyclodextrin glycosyltransferase (derived from bacteria such as Bacillus macerans) on starch.

questions.question_text: Florentine receiver is used to separate the liquids based on
questions.explanation: A Florentine receiver separates immiscible liquids of different densities, such as volatile oils from water in steam distillation.

questions.question_text: The official dissolution test apparatus contains cylindrical vessel and lower edge of the blade is positioned from inside bottom vessel at
questions.explanation: According to USP guidelines for dissolution apparatus 2 (paddle), the distance between the blade and the inside bottom of the vessel is $25 \pm 2 \text{ mm}$ ($23$ to $27 \text{ mm}$).

questions.question_text: As per Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules, the Good Manufacturing Practice is included under schedule
questions.explanation: Schedule M of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act covers GMP requirements for pharmaceutical manufacturing.

questions.question_text: A substance used for modification of silica gel for reversed-phase TLC is
questions.explanation: Impregnating silica gel with silicone oil or paraffin creates a reversed-phase thin-layer chromatographic plate.

questions.question_text: In IR spectrum, the functional group region is from
questions.explanation: The functional group region in an infrared (IR) spectrum typically spans from $4000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ to $1400 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

questions.question_text: The equation $E = E^0 + \frac{RT}{nF} \ln a_{M^{n+}}$ is used to measure the
questions.explanation: The Nernst equation calculates the cell potential or electrode potential difference.

questions.question_text: Intermediates in the biosynthesis of cholesterol are
questions.explanation: Mevalonate and isopentenyl pyrophosphate (IPP) are key intermediates in the mevalonate pathway leading to cholesterol biosynthesis.

questions.question_text: A naturally occurring amino acid which does not have a chiral centre is
questions.explanation: Glycine has two hydrogen atoms attached to its alpha carbon, making it achiral.

questions.question_text: A given Gram-positive bacterium is differentiated from Gram-negative by Gram staining. This is because its cell wall contains
questions.explanation: Gram-positive cell walls contain a thick peptidoglycan layer associated with teichoic acids, which helps retain the crystal violet-iodine complex.

questions.question_text: The drug which increases the plasma concentration of digoxin by a pharmacokinetic mechanism is
questions.explanation: Quinidine displaces digoxin from tissue binding sites and reduces its renal clearance, significantly increasing plasma digoxin concentration.

questions.question_text: Microscopic characters of ginger rhizome are

options.A: Spindle shaped lignified fibers and sclereids
options.B: Cluster crystals of calcium oxalate and sclereids
options.C: Non-lignified vessels and sac shaped starch grains

questions.explanation: Ginger rhizome histology typically shows abundant starch grains, oil cells, and non-lignified fibers, alongside cluster crystals of calcium oxalate and occasional sclereids.

questions.question_text: Klunge's test is for the identification of
questions.explanation: Klunge's test is a specific chemical test used to identify isobarbaloin in aloes.

questions.question_text: 3,4 Benzpyrene present in cigarette smoke reduces the therapeutic activity of Diazepam by

options.D: Increasing the activity of liver microsomal enzymes

questions.explanation: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons like 3,4-benzpyrene induce hepatic CYP enzymes (such as CYP1A2), increasing the metabolism and reducing the effectiveness of drugs like diazepam.

questions.question_text: An NMDA antagonist introduced for treatment of Alzheimer's disease is
questions.explanation: Memantine is a low-affinity uncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist used for moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: Reaction: 2,4-dichloroquinazoline + Hydrazine hydrate (< 20°C for 1 hr in pyridine) -> Resulting product treated with NaOH at 100°C for 1 hr gave an effective product for the treatment of Gout. Identity

options.A: Structure with OH on quinazoline ring
options.C: Structure with hydroxy group at position 4

questions.explanation: The reaction sequence yields a fused triazoloquinazoline derivative useful in gout therapy (such as an analog or related xanthine oxidase inhibitor synthesis).

questions.question_text: Phenol, an antiseptic when treated as follows: Phenol + C6H5COCl -> Phenyl benzoate (OCOC2H5 typo/analog) + AlCl3,CS2 -> gives two phenolic ketones. The reaction is
questions.explanation: The conversion of a phenyl ester into an ortho- and/or para-hydroxyketone in the presence of a Lewis acid like AlCl3 is the Fries rearrangement.

questions.question_text: The quantity of drug required to make a 2% w/w solution in 240ml of alcohol is (The density of alcohol is $0.816 \text{ g/ml}$)
questions.explanation: Mass of alcohol = $240 \text{ ml} \times 0.816 \text{ g/ml} = 195.84 \text{ g}$. For a 2% w/w solution, mass of drug = $195.84 \times 0.02 / 0.98 \approx 4.0 \text{ g}$ or directly taking $2\% \times 240 \times 0.816 = 3.918 \text{ g}$ close to $4 \text{ g}$.

questions.question_text: In multistation punching machine, the upper as well as lower punches are connected by
questions.explanation: In a rotary tablet press (multistation punching machine), the punches are held and guided by upper and lower turrets.

questions.question_text: As per the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, the HEPA filters are required to filter the air in the pharmaceutical manufacturing unit. Grade A filter is used for

options.B: Background room used for preliminary activities

questions.explanation: Grade A laminar airflow zones are used for high-risk operations such as aseptic connection and filling.

questions.question_text: The deflection of positive ions formed in a mass spectrometer by electric and magnetic fields depends upon its
questions.explanation: The trajectory and deflection of ions in combined electric and magnetic fields depend on mass, charge, and initial velocity parameters.

questions.question_text: Cyclohexane can be used as a solvent in UV spectrophotometric analysis because

options.B: Energy requirement for $\sigma - \sigma^*$ is in the range of $120-200 \text{ nm}$

questions.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons like cyclohexane absorb only in the vacuum UV region (below $200 \text{ nm}$) due to high-energy $\sigma - \sigma^*$ transitions, making them transparent in the near-UV range.

questions.question_text: Quaternary structure in protein molecules refers to the

options.A: Arrangement of multiple domains in a single polypeptide chain
options.B: Specific arrangement of multiple subunits in multi-subunit proteins
options.D: Protein folding in single subunit proteins

questions.explanation: Quaternary structure describes the assembly and spatial arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits in a multimeric protein.

questions.question_text: Interleukins are

options.A: Polypeptide cytokines important in the inflammatory cascade
options.B: Prostaglandins that account for gastrointestinal disorders
options.C: Enkephalins which are specific for asthma

questions.explanation: Interleukins are a group of cytokine proteins that play crucial roles in the immune system and inflammatory pathways.

questions.question_text: Phase I clinical studies of a drug under development is generally carried out on

options.A: At least 10,000 people from different ethnic communities and a wide range of age groups
options.B: A medium sized group of 500-1000 patients suffering from the disease for which the drug is being developed
options.C: A small group of 20-100 healthy male and female volunteers
options.D: Reliable in-vitro cell-lines derived from people suffering with the disease

questions.explanation: Phase I clinical trials primarily evaluate safety, pharmacokinetics, and tolerability in a small group of healthy volunteers (usually 20-100).

questions.question_text: A young patient complains that he gets severe shortness of breath whenever he takes aspirin for headache. Increased levels of a substance responsible for aspirin hypersensitivity is
questions.explanation: Aspirin-induced asthma occurs because COX inhibition shunts arachidonic acid down the lipoxygenase pathway, leading to an overproduction of bronchoconstrictive leukotrienes (e.g., LTC4/LTD4).

questions.question_text: Match group I with group II and identify the correct combinations: Group I (Glycoside: (P) Gentisin, (Q) Genistein, (R) Apigenin, (S) Quercetin) with Group II (Type: 1. Flavonol, 2. Flavone, 3. Xanthone, 4. Isoflavon)
questions.explanation: Gentisin is a xanthone (P-3), Genistein is an isoflavone (Q-4), Apigenin is a flavone (R-2), and Quercetin is a flavonol (S-1).

questions.question_text: Match Group I (Bark Diagnostic: (P) Kurchi, (Q) Cascara, (R) Cinnamon, (S) Cinchona) with Group II (Microscopical Characters)
questions.explanation: Matching the characteristic bark microscopy keys gives P-2, Q-1, R-4, S-3.

questions.question_text: Match Group I (Drug: (P) Levofloxacin, (Q) Caspofungin, (R) Aztreonam, (S) Rifabutin) with Group II (Mechanism of action is by inhibition of)
questions.explanation: Levofloxacin inhibits DNA gyrase/topoisomerase II (P-2), Caspofungin inhibits beta(1-2) glucan (Q-3), Aztreonam binds specific PBP (R-4), and Rifabutin inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (S-1).

questions.question_text: Match Group I (Drug: (P) Granisetron, (Q) Pirenzepine, (R) Acebutalol, (S) Baclofen) with Group II (Receptor agonist/antagonist)
questions.explanation: Granisetron is a 5-HT3 antagonist (P-3), Pirenzepine is an M1 antagonist (Q-4), Acebutolol is a beta-1 antagonist (R-1), and Baclofen is a GABA agonist (S-2).

questions.question_text: Match Group I (Drug: (P) Chlorpromazine, (Q) Thioridazine, (R) Diazepam, (S) Thiopentone) with Group II (Biotransformation)
questions.explanation: Matching primary biotransformation pathways for these CNS agents gives P-4, Q-1, R-2, S-3.

questions.question_text: Match Group I (Drug: (P) Diprophylline, (Q) Ethophylline, (R) Etamiphylline, (S) Proxyphylline) with Group II (7-Substitution in 1,3-dimethyl xanthine structures)
questions.explanation: Diprophylline has a dihydroxypropyl substituent (1), Etamiphylline has an aminoethyl substituent (4), proxyphylline has another variant, matching to D.
